title: Ivo and the Typewriter
premise: In 1938, in the mountain town of Vell, apprentice clockmaker Dominic Reyes is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock and finds, wedged inside its case, a typewriter whose ribbon holds the typed confession of a dead magistrate documenting the governor's theft of the valley's land deeds. When the season's first snows close the bridge — the only road out — Dominic realizes the governor will burn the evidence and everyone who touched it. Over one frozen week he smuggles the typed pages past three checkpoints with the help of the magistrate's widow, Elka, who teaches him that history is not something that happens elsewhere. The book ends with Dominic mailing the confession from the far side of the bridge as the clock above the town strikes a repaired, honest hour — and with him choosing to stay, no longer invisible.
about_author: Casper Ishikawa is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing municipal records in small alpine towns, where he learned that the most dangerous documents are the ones nobody was meant to keep. He writes historical fiction about ordinary people caught holding evidence they cannot put down.

chapters.title: The Hour That Would Not Hold
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Summoned to the observatory, he repairs the master clock and discovers the typewriter hidden in its case, its ribbon still inked with a dead magistrate's confession naming the governor. He tells himself it is not his business. Emotional beat: the uneasy thrill of a man who wants to remain a bystander but has already touched the evidence.

chapters.title: What the Bridge Keeps Out
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The snows close the bridge; the governor's men begin searching houses for the magistrate's papers. Elka, the widow, confronts Dominic, revealing the confession implicates the family that employs him. He hides the pages inside the clock's weights. Emotional beat: fear curdling into complicity — staying invisible is now itself a choice with victims.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Alternating Dominic's and Elka's POVs. The smuggling plan unfolds: the pages travel in pieces — inside a repaired watch, a hymnal, a sack of clock oil — past the tavern, the toll house, and the governor's own clerk. The clerk recognizes Dominic's workmanship and hesitates, then lets him pass. Emotional beat: rising tension and the discovery that power corrupts quietly, one small mercy and one small betrayal at a time.

chapters.title: An Honest Hour
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. At the bridge, the governor himself waits, offering Dominic apprenticeship, inheritance, silence. Dominic refuses, mails the confession, and returns across the ice as the town below hears the master clock strike true for the first time in years. Emotional beat: quiet triumph and transformation — a boy who believed history happened elsewhere learns he has just made some.
